practices.practice: Load the cluster connection string from an environment variable (do not hard-code or commit it), avoid printing the full URI to logs, and use an example file (.env.example) or a secret store for developer onboarding.
practices.prior_belief: Load the cluster connection string from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime, never hard-code or check the secret into source control, and do not log the full URI; use a .env.example with a placeholder instead.

practices.practice: Tune MongoDB driver connection options to your deployment: set sensible maxPoolSize/minPoolSize, serverSelectionTimeoutMS and socketTimeoutMS according to serverless vs long-running server patterns, and choose timeouts that fail fast for your topology.
practices.prior_belief: Open the Mongoose/Mongo driver with explicit modern options: useNewUrlParser: true, useUnifiedTopology: true, serverSelectionTimeoutMS: 5000, socketTimeoutMS: 600000, maxPoolSize: 50 and set an appName; include retryWrites=true in the connection string if supported.

practices.practice: Use a single MongoClient / Mongoose connection (singleton) for the process and reuse it across requests; in serverless functions create the client at module scope so warm invocations reuse the pool.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid opening many separate connections or one change stream per user; run a single shared change-stream watcher (per process) and fan-out events internally or partition by logical key if you must scale horizontally; tune maxPoolSize to match concurrency.

practices.practice: Always require TLS when connecting to Azure DocumentDB; do not disable certificate verification in production and ensure the connection string includes tls=true (or equivalent driver TLS options).

When using change streams and you need the post-update document, open the stream with fullDocument: 'updateLookup' (or use the $changeStream stage with fullDocument option) so handlers receive the current document on update events.

practices.practice: Persist change-stream resume tokens durably (save the _id token after processing events) and resume the stream with resumeAfter/startAtOperationTime to continue from the last processed event; historical replay is supported via startAtOperationTime when available.
practices.prior_belief: When using change streams, call watch() with fullDocument: 'updateLookup' if your alert evaluation needs the full current document, persist the latest resumeToken to durable storage after each processed change, and on restart try to resume using that token (with exponential backoff and jitter if resume fails).

practices.practice: Keep change-stream handlers short and avoid heavy synchronous work in the watch loop; offload webhook delivery or expensive evaluation to background workers/queues and process historical checkpoints during low-traffic windows to reduce impact on live streams.
practices.prior_belief: Keep change-stream handlers short and nonblocking: push webhook delivery and heavy alert evaluation to a background worker or message queue so the watch loop can acknowledge/resume quickly and avoid large event-processing latencies or timeouts.

practices.practice: Design alert-rule queries so they can be satisfied by indexes (e.g., lookup by userId + active + symbol); create appropriate compound indexes rather than scanning all rules.
practices.prior_belief: Design alert rule documents so they can be looked up by assetId (or symbol) and active flag; create a compound index on { assetId: 1, active: 1 } so the change-stream handler can quickly find only relevant rules for an updated position rather than scanning all rules.

practices.practice: Follow the ESR rule (Equality → Sort → Range) when creating compound indexes for queries and aggregation match stages, and prefer one well-designed compound index over multiple single-field indexes.

Create indexes to support aggregation match and group stages used by portfolio P&L and sector allocation (e.g., indexes on accountId, symbol, sector or a compound {accountId:1, symbol:1}) to avoid collection scans and speed aggregation.
practices.prior_belief: Add indexes to support your aggregation match stages—e.g., for portfolio P&L and sector allocation create indexes on { accountId: 1 }, { symbol: 1 }, and { sector: 1 } (or a compound index { accountId: 1, symbol: 1 }) so $match and $group stages run without full-collection scans; build indexes idempotently via a script.

practices.practice: When running potentially large aggregations, enable allowDiskUse: true and minimize projection/result shape to reduce data transferred over the wire; test with realistic datasets.
practices.prior_belief: Use aggregation options allowDiskUse: true for potentially large portfolio aggregations, and limit aggregation pipeline result shapes and projections so documents transferred over the wire are minimal; test aggregate with realistic dataset sizes.

practices.practice: Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient connection/server-selection errors and rate-limited responses (e.g., handle MongoNetworkError/MongoServerSelectionError and 429), and cap retries with a dead-lettering approach for permanent failures.
practices.prior_belief: Implement retry with exponential backoff and jitter for transient MongoNetworkError/MongoServerSelectionError and for webhook delivery; cap retries and surface permanent failures to an operator queue or dead-letter store.

practices.practice: Make seed scripts idempotent by using upserts keyed on stable natural keys (e.g., userId+symbol for positions, rule unique attributes for alert rules) so seeds can be rerun safely.
practices.prior_belief: Make seeding/idempotent: seed scripts should upsert by a stable natural key (e.g., symbol+accountId for positions, ruleId for alert rules) so they can be run repeatedly without creating duplicates.

practices.practice: Model and store embeddings as a fixed-length numeric array and record the embedding dimensionality and model metadata; for cosine similarity, normalize embeddings client-side so index and query similarity behave predictably.
practices.prior_belief: Model embeddings for vector search as a fixed-length array of floats under a named field (e.g., embedding: [Number]), store the vector dimensionality explicitly in the schema, and normalize vectors client-side if using cosine similarity so index/search behave predictably.

practices.practice: Create a dedicated vector index (cosmosSearch) with explicit options (kind: vector-diskann/hnsw/ivf, dimensions, similarity, maxDegree, lBuild) that match your embedding model and scale; mismatched dimensions or similarity silently break results.
practices.prior_belief: Create a dedicated vector index with explicit parameters (indexType: 'HNSW' or 'IVF', similarity: 'cosine' or 'dot', dimensions: N, efConstruction and M for HNSW) via the cluster's index API or createIndex extension rather than relying on a default B-tree index for embedding fields.

practices.practice: Enable diagnostic settings and capture slow-query logs to Log Analytics (or Event Hub/Storage) and alert on CPU, memory, IOPS, storage, and connection saturation so you can find unindexed queries and diagnose performance regressions.
practices.prior_belief: Instrument and monitor latency, server selection, connection pool metrics, and slow queries; on Azure enable Diagnostic Settings / Azure Monitor for the cluster and capture MongoDB slow query logs and server metrics so you can correlate alerts triggered by data with database performance.

practices.practice: Pick cluster throughput (provisioned or autoscale) to cover peak workloads from change-stream consumers and heavy aggregations; test and size for the aggregate and change-stream load rather than relying solely on default tiers.
practices.prior_belief: Choose provisioned throughput (or autoscale) to cover peak workloads from the change-stream watcher and occasional large aggregations; for Cosmos-based services configure RU/s or autoscale so long-running aggregations won't be throttled, and design aggregations to run during off-peak windows if necessary.

practices.practice: Rely on the platform's automatic backups (continuous for active clusters) and retention policy (35 days for active clusters) as part of DR planning; use backups and cross-region replicas to implement your recovery runbooks.
practices.prior_belief: Back up critical collections (positions, alertrules) regularly and ensure your backup/restore process preserves resumeTokens if you need point-in-time replay; enable the platform backup (continuous or periodic) offered by Azure for production.

practices.practice: Prefer network isolation (Private Endpoint / firewall rules) and Microsoft Entra ID + RBAC for auth and use customer-managed keys (CMK) for encryption-at-rest when required by compliance.
Make webhook delivery idempotent (include an event id or deduplication key and have the receiver deduplicate), or persist short-lived delivery records so retries don't cause duplicate effects.
practices.prior_belief: Make webhook delivery idempotent: include an event id (change _id or resume token) and have the webhook receiver deduplicate, or persist a short-lived delivery record on the service side so retries won't produce duplicate actions.

practices.practice: When using Mongoose in read-heavy code paths, prefer projection + .lean() (or raw driver queries) to avoid constructing Mongoose documents when you only need plain objects for evaluation/aggregation.
practices.prior_belief: Use schema-level projections and .lean() in read-heavy aggregation and query helpers (Mongoose) to avoid building full Mongoose documents when you only need plain objects for aggregation/evaluation.
